messages:
andrea.s: quick sanity check — I opened a small TF change that adds a KMS key + IRSA role for the secrets-store CSI driver + ExternalSecrets. after applying pods that mount the secret can't decrypt, getting `AccessDenied` from KMS. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/2487 :wave:

sam: looking — do you create a `aws_kms_grant` referencing the role ARN? those can fail if the role doesn't exist yet at apply time. paste the snippets?

andrea.s: sure. here's the relevant bits — simplified:
```hcl
module "irsa_external_secrets" {
  source = "./modules/irsa"
  sa_name = "external-secrets-sa"
}
resource "aws_kms_key" "secrets" {
  description = "keys for secrets-store"
}
resource "aws_kms_grant" "for_irsa" {
  name = "external-secrets-grant"
  key_id = aws_kms_key.secrets.key_id
  grantee_principal = module.irsa_external_secrets.role_arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
}
```

sam: yeah that's the classic ordering hazard — TF tries to create the grant while the role ARN might be a computed value that isn't available yet. also if the assumption policy for the role has the wrong OIDC audience/issuer the token won't let it assume.

maria: another angle: the secrets-store CSI driver (or ESO) will assume the role via the KSA annotation `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn`. confirm the serviceaccount annotation exists in the same namespace and that the OIDC provider in the account matches the `sub` claim pattern in your role trust policy.

andrea.s: annotation is there, e.g. `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: ${module.irsa_external_secrets.role_arn}` in the K8s manifest. OIDC provider was created last year by infra.

devex: quick checklist I usually run: 1) role assume policy StringEquals for `${oidc_provider}:sub` matches `system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa>` 2) `aud` is `sts.amazonaws.com` 3) role exists before `aws_kms_grant` creation or use a key policy instead of grant 4) confirm key policy allows the role to use the key (grants are fine but key policy must not explicitly deny)

sam: either put the grant creation into the same module that creates the role (so TF knows ordering) or add an explicit `depends_on = [module.irsa_external_secrets]` on `aws_kms_grant`. that usually fixes apply-order. downside: if module returns role_arn as a computed value that changes, grant may re-create.

andrea.s: good point. I moved grant into the key module to be closer to the role but still hit the same error. added `depends_on = [module.irsa_external_secrets]` and re-applied — still failing with `AccessDenied`.

maria: hmm — when you say AccessDenied, is the KMS error message `not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt` for principal `arn:aws:sts::...:assumed-role/.../...`? if it's the assumed-role principal, that means the pod had a token and AWS issued temporary creds, but KMS denied. share the logs?

andrea.s: log snippet from pod:
```
Error getting secret: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/IRSA-external-secrets-role/i-123456 is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh
```

sam: the principal shown is an assumed-role (good). Now check the key policy — if the key policy only allows accounts or a different principal, grants won't work as expected. Also check if the grant's `grantee_principal` used the role ARN or role ID — it should be the role ARN.

devex: also ensure `encryption_context` is not enforced by the key policy or your client request. If ESO/CSI sends an encryption context that doesn't match policy, KMS will deny. not common, but worth checking.

andrea.s: key policy currently is pretty open (account root + a list of ARNs). grant shows status `Active` in console and lists the role ARN as grantee. I suspect the key policy might still block `kms:Decrypt` for that assumed-role because the policy only allows `aws:PrincipalArn` equals role arn (not assumed-role arn).

maria: yes, remember that when STS issues creds you get `arn:aws:sts::acct:assumed-role/role-name/session-name`. If your key policy condition checks `PrincipalArn` exactly for `role/role-name` it won't match the assumed-role. Better to grant `kms:Decrypt` to the role principal in the key policy or use `aws:PrincipalIsAWSService` style statements. Grants normally handle assumed-role, but key policy needs to allow use by principals in general.

sam: quick mitigation: add a key policy statement allowing `arn:aws:iam::<acct>:role/IRSA-external-secrets-role` and also allow assumed-role ARNs using a wildcard: `arn:aws:sts::<acct>:assumed-role/IRSA-external-secrets-role/*` or use `Principal` = { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::<acct>:role/IRSA-external-secrets-role" } without condition — test in staging.

andrea.s: ah ok that matches the console error. I can try updating key policy to include the assumed-role pattern, or change grant to use `GranteePrincipal` of the assumed-role (but that varies).

devex: one more Terraform tip: if you want deterministic ordering, pass the role name/arn into the key module as an input param and then create the grant there. avoid referencing `module.irsa_external_secrets.role_arn` indirectly — make it explicit so the graph picks it up.

andrea.s: thanks — I'll: (1) add the assumed-role wildcard to key policy in staging, (2) move grant creation to role module and wire role_arn via input, (3) reapply and report back.

sam: ping me if it still fails. also consider using a key policy that delegates use to the account and then rely on IAM for fine-grained access — simpler for service accounts.

infra-bot: deploy queued: infra/staging apply starting for PR #2487 — monitor logs at https://ci.redwood.dev/2487

andrea.s: applying now — will post results. :thumbsup:
